name: Hell-Ville
tagline: The administrative town, properly called Andoany
description: The island's main town at the southeastern corner, with the market, the banks, the port and the colonial-era buildings left from the French period. Almost nothing here is aimed at visitors, which is exactly why prices are what they are.
bestFor: Anyone needing banks, the market or the ferry, and local prices
pros: Cheapest food and accommodation on the island
The port and the boats to the mainland

name: Ambatoloaka
tagline: The tourist strip on the west coast
description: A beach village on the western shore that has become the island's concentration of hotels, dive shops, restaurants and bars, and the departure point for most of the boat trips. It is where nearly every visitor to Nosy Be stays.
bestFor: Anyone who wants dive operators and restaurants on the doorstep
pros: All the dive shops and boat operators
Restaurants and bars along the beach
Easy to arrange trips to the other islands
cons: The most touristed spot on the island
The bar scene is not to everyone's taste

name: Madirokely and Ambondrona
description: The bays immediately north of Ambatoloaka, with the same west-facing sunsets and a considerably quieter feel, a scattering of small hotels and a beach that is better for swimming. Ten minutes on foot from the main strip.
bestFor: Anyone wanting the coast without Ambatoloaka's intensity
pros: Walking distance to the dive shops
cons: Transport needed for the rest of the island

name: Mont Passot and the Crater Lakes
tagline: The high ground with the sacred lakes
description: The island's highest point, with a series of crater lakes below it that are sacred to the Sakalava and carry real restrictions on behaviour, and the viewpoint that gives Nosy Be its best sunset. It is inland and rural.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the interior rather than the beach strip
pros: The island's best views and sunsets
Cooler and away from the tourist coast
cons: Local taboos on the lakes must be respected

name: Lokobe and the East Coast
tagline: The reserve side, with the lemurs
description: The southeastern corner of the island holding the Lokobe Strict Reserve, one of the last patches of Sambirano lowland rainforest, reached by pirogue from Ambatozavavy. Black lemurs, chameleons and boa constrictors live in it.
bestFor: Anyone who came to Madagascar for the wildlife
pros: Black lemurs and chameleons in genuine forest
cons: Access is by boat and guide only
